terms.comment: Lewis & Short: rare of physical things; in good prose of joining things in the mind, and of bonds between people (friendship, marriage, kinship). In grammar it is a conjunction. Where English says “a combination of A and B”, Latin often says A cum B conjūnctum.

evidence: Petr. 94: rāram facit mixtūram cum sapientiā fōrma (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short’s headword is mistūra. For ingredients, colours, qualities; Lewis & Short also records a sexual sense (Luc., Plin.).

phrases.latin: rāram facit mixtūram cum sapientiā fōrma
phrases.english: beauty is rarely found in combination with wisdom

phrases.latin: hanc mixtūram cum in catillō composueris, oleum superfunditō
phrases.english: when you have put this mixture in a bowl, pour oil over it

phrases.latin: bene enim majōrēs accubitiōnem epulārem amīcōrum, quia vītae conjūnctiōnem habēret, convīvium nōmināvērunt
phrases.english: our ancestors did well to call friends’ dining together a convivium, because it is a joining of lives

sources: Lewis & Short: conjunctio · Lewis & Short: mistura · Lewis & Short: conjungo
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cato (Columella), loci-cicero-philosophica), checked against the editions named there.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
